tier_reason: Independent third-party shootout (jamboree/CxxFunctionBenchmark, code in various.cpp + measure.hpp) times stdext::inplace_function<int(int),40> against std::function side by side; compiler stated (MSVC 64-bit VS 15.9.4, Release Build) but no exact flags or CPU model, so short of A. All seven inplace_function vs std::function timings in the record match the README rows exactly.

corrections.workload: CxxFunctionBenchmark various.cpp: invocation-only timing of int(int) type-erased wrappers (callable assigned once in the fixture constructor, then invoked repeatedly) across 7 callable kinds; inplace_function instantiated as stdext::inplace_function<int(int), 40>
corrections.caveats: Mixed shootout results and small margins: wins by ~2% (heavy_functor) to ~20% (compile_time_delegate), loses in lambda_capture (0.1851s vs 0.1757s) and stateless_lambda (0.1845s vs 0.1799s). The benchmark times invocation only, not construction or allocation. Only MSVC STL tested; flags given only as 'Release Build' and no CPU model, capping tier at B. inplace_function.h is one header inside the multi-proposal SG14 monorepo; repo-level GitHub license field is empty, but the header carries a Boost Software License 1.0 notice.

notes: Numbers verified row-by-row against the README raw text; the benchmark copies an SG14 inplace_function.h (BSL-1.0 header, namespace stdext). Removed unsupported caveat claim that losses stem from std::function avoiding heap allocation (benchmark measures calls only). Metadata (535 stars, last commit 2022-04-19, not archived, not a fork) confirmed; B-tier rests on treating CxxFunctionBenchmark (98 stars) as a well-known independent suite.

tier_reason: First-party Google Benchmark code is public (smallfun/apps/main.cpp) and .buckconfig sets cxxflags '-O3 -Os -Ofast', compilers named (g++6, clang++6/libc++), but no CPU model is stated, so it cannot be A; being first-party, it is C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README claims SmallFun is '3-5x faster than std::function' in some benchmarks. Table (ns, lower is better): std::function 1141 ns (g++6) / 1511 ns (clang++6 & libc++) vs sf32 312/300, sf64 369/310, sf128 346/333, sf256 376/320, sf512 503/450, sf1024 569/512, sf2048 870/709. That is about 3.0-3.7x (g++6) and 4.5-5.0x (clang) for 32-256-byte buffers, falling to 1.3x (g++6) / 2.1x (clang) at sf2048 (derived from page data)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: g++6 and clang++6/libc++; repo .buckconfig sets cxxflags = -O3 -Os -Ofast
corrections.workload: Google Benchmark: assign 100 identical small lambdas (capture int i, unsigned N) into a vector of std::function or SmallFun<..., B> (B = 32-2048 byte buffer), then invoke all via std::transform, per iteration
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark; flags come from .buckconfig (-O3 -Os -Ofast) but no CPU model is stated, so tier is capped at C. The speedup shrinks with larger buffers (1.3x g++6 at sf2048). SmallFun rejects at compile time (enable_if) any callable larger than its fixed buffer; there is no heap fallback. No commits since January 2018.

notes: Numbers match the README table. The record's '3.1-4.9x depending on buffer size/compiler' range covers only sf64 and overstates the low end (real range 1.3-5.0x across buffers), so claimed_speedup is corrected; tier stays C. Metadata verified: MIT, 54 stars, last commit 2018-01-04, not archived or a fork.
